spec.title: z.ai GLM through Claude Code — parent/worker protocol

p.SCOPE: This protocol governs a parent agent in any harness that commissions z.ai GLM workers through the ordinary Claude Code CLI. It covers launcher configuration, task routing, cwd/session identity, packets, reports, observation, terminal-state classification, recovery and acceptance. It does not grant a worker central authority, prescribe one repository's Cargo limits, or promise that a provider quota remains open.

p.PORTABLE-CORE: The same process contract binds a Claude parent and a Codex parent. Harness adapters differ only in how they start and observe a child process; packet bytes, worker authority, cwd, launcher, deliverables and acceptance are identical.

p.PARENT-AUTHORITY: The parent owns architecture, public semantics, unresolved ambiguity, destructive decisions, write-set routing, acceptance, staging, commits, integration and final gates. A GLM worker executes or advises; it never promotes its own result.

p.DELEGATION-CALCULUS: Delegate when independent verification is cheaper than generation. Prefer GLM for substantial, explicit work with a cheap oracle, broad local extraction and templated mechanical transformations. Keep tiny deterministic edits and ambiguity that is the design parent-side. Difficulty and volume are not reasons to weaken the intended solution.

p.ADVISORY-REVIEW: An independent GLM review is useful evidence, but authoritative acceptance review remains parent-side. Model diversity counts only when the review names exact evidence and the parent reproduces the decisive claim.

p.INSTALL-THEN-DEPLOY: Package materialisation and user-state deployment are separate phases. `vibe install` brings the package protocol into the project. The package's explicit host deploy profile, run against its resolved slot, publishes `claudez.ps1` plus `claudez.cmd` for `windows`, or executable `claudez` for `posix`, under `<settings-root>/opt/bin`; default settings make that `~/.vibe/opt/bin`. Until target OS applicability lands, no default profile is declared or inferred. Receipts, drift checks, recovery and undeploy belong to the deploy engine.

p.NO-INSTALL-HOOK-COPY: Never replace the deploy phase with a post-install hook or manual copy. Those paths lose receipt ownership, collision detection, recovery and inverse operation.

p.PATH-NOT-MUTATED: The package does not edit PATH. The operator or surrounding VibeVM installation owns whether `<settings-root>/opt/bin` is already discoverable; with default settings that path is `~/.vibe/opt/bin`. A parent may always invoke the launcher by absolute path.

facts.LAUNCHER-THIN: The launcher validates prerequisites, constructs one child environment and returns the exact child exit. The PowerShell and Bash forms preserve the caller's argument vector; the Bash form replaces its own process with `exec`, and PowerShell restores every process environment member it temporarily replaced. `claudez.cmd` is a command-shell convenience shim and therefore has ordinary `cmd.exe` reparsing semantics; callers needing exact empty or pathological quoting/ backslash arguments invoke `claudez.ps1` directly. No form contains scheduling, packet parsing, retry or acceptance policy.
facts.LAUNCHER-CLAUDE-FIRST: Resolve the Claude Code command before reading a credential. Missing Claude fails with a remediation and no credential read.
facts.LAUNCHER-TOKEN: The token source defaults to `~/.vibe/zai.api.token` and may be overridden by `ZAI_API_TOKEN_FILE`. Missing or empty input fails closed. Errors may print the source path, never the value.
facts.LAUNCHER-ENDPOINT: The endpoint defaults to the z.ai Anthropic-compatible HTTPS origin. Any `ZAI_GLM_BASE_URL` override is trusted operator configuration but still must be an absolute HTTPS URL with a nonempty host and no userinfo or fragment. Validate it before opening the token source, so invalid routing cannot expose a bearer.
facts.LAUNCHER-STATE: State defaults to `~/.claude-glm`; `ZAI_GLM_CONFIG_DIR` and the compatibility alias `CLAUDEZ_CONFIG_DIR` may override it. Persistent isolated state is what makes exact-cwd continuation possible without contaminating the user's ordinary Claude state.
facts.LAUNCHER-MODELS: The current defaults request `glm-5.3[1m]` for Claude's Opus/Sonnet aliases and `glm-5-turbo` for the Haiku alias. `ZAI_GLM_BIG_MODEL` and `ZAI_GLM_SMALL_MODEL` override the requests. These strings are configuration, never proof of the resolved model.
facts.LAUNCHER-RUNTIME: The default endpoint is `https://api.z.ai/api/anthropic`, timeout is `3000000` ms, thinking budget request is `32000`, and nonessential Claude traffic is disabled. The corresponding `ZAI_GLM_BASE_URL`, `ZAI_GLM_API_TIMEOUT_MS` and `ZAI_GLM_MAX_THINKING` settings are explicit overrides; legacy `CLAUDEZ_MAX_THINKING` remains a lower-precedence compatibility input.

p.CONFIG-SOURCES-NOT-SECRETS: Configuration sources, model request strings and paths may be reported. Credential contents may not. A worker packet never asks the worker to inspect its own provider environment.

p.CONVERSATION-KEY: Continuation identity is the pair `(CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, cwd)`. A different launcher state directory or cwd is a different conversation even when the prompt text is identical.

facts.ONE-WRITER-PER-CWD: One cwd has at most one live writing worker. Read-only reviewers may overlap; writers with intersecting product paths are serialized.
facts.SCOPED-CWD: Pin cwd in the process launch or a scoped `Push-Location`/subshell. Never use a persistent bare `cd`: it silently retargets every later correction, not only the next command.
facts.FRESH: Fresh work uses `claudez -p <pointer>`. The pointer names the packet and repeats the visible-artifact/report/no- commit invariants.
facts.CONTINUE: A correction uses `claudez -c -p <correction>` only after the prior process is terminal and from the exact original cwd. It repairs named findings; it does not defend the prior verdict.

p.PACKET-FILE: Large context travels in a file inside the worker cwd, never as a giant command argument. Every named input must actually exist in that cwd or be an explicit readable absolute path.

facts.PACKET-ROLE: Name worker role and the authority it does not have.
facts.PACKET-TASK: State one bounded outcome and the exact required inputs.
facts.PACKET-PERIMETER: Close the expected write perimeter; permit only reasoned, nonintersecting expansion disclosed in the report.
facts.PACKET-ACCEPTANCE: Name observable success, compatibility and failure/negative criteria. Empty output needs a positive control proving the instrument can fire.
facts.PACKET-VERIFY: List narrow self-verification commands and preserve the gate child's real exit. A broad substitute or piped tail is not equivalent.
facts.PACKET-HANDOFF: Leave product work as ordinary visible unstaged files plus a durable report. No commit, index, stash, hidden worktree, patch-only copy or external-only deliverable.

p.NORMAL-TOOLS: Launch with an explicit noninteractive permission mode and a normal task-capable tool surface. Read/search tools, shell, read-only Git archaeology, formatters, generators and exact tests are ordinary worker instruments. A tiny allow-list is appropriate only when the restriction itself is the experiment.

p.HANDOFF-IS-SAFETY: Safety comes from a bounded packet, dedicated cwd, visible unstaged handoff and parent review—not from starving a capable worker of the tools required to reason.

p.REPORT-SKELETON-EARLY: Create the report skeleton after the first meaningful product slice, with every not-yet-run gate marked `PENDING`. Update it before long tests. Turn caps, provider limits and process loss can end the next call.

p.REPORT-SHAPE: A normal implementation report targets roughly 140 lines and caps at 150 unless a large evidence matrix genuinely needs more. It contains: advisory verdict; exact changed files and why; criterion-by-criterion evidence; negative/RED proofs; commands with real exits and counts; decisions; perimeter expansion/external effects; and exact leftovers.

p.REPORT-NOT-VERDICT: The report reduces acceptance cost but cannot replace it. Screen `PASS`, `TASK-DONE`, a confident summary and a green producer test remain advisory.

p.OUTPUT-POLICY: For long runs through a parent process tool, prefer ordinary text output plus the bounded report. Stream JSON is useful for a short metadata probe or when redirected to a file outside model ingestion; feeding thinking-token events back into context wastes the parent budget and may fill pipes.

facts.TERMINAL-RESULT: When structured output exists, its terminal result plus process exit is authoritative transport state. Grep hits for `TASK-DONE`, log size and mtime are not: prompt text and thinking telemetry can produce all three.
facts.GLM-IDENTITY-PROOF: A test claiming that GLM executed must inspect the separate child process's terminal metadata. For current Claude Code JSON, a nonempty `modelUsage` key set names the models that served the run; the proof requires GLM identities there plus a nonempty child `session_id`. The packet also asks the worker which model it is and requires that self-report to equal one of the independently observed usage keys. Either half alone is insufficient. Parent-created artifacts or a configured alias cannot establish which model executed.
facts.OBSERVE-LIVE: Judge liveness from the exact process, last non-telemetry event, visible artifact changes and report progress. None alone is completion.
facts.TERMINAL-COMPLETE: Normal terminal success means the transport ended; inspect deliverables before any code verdict.
facts.TERMINAL-ERROR: Gateway error, 429, timeout and account exhaustion are provider state. Confirm once; do not spin retries.
facts.TERMINAL-CAP: Turn-cap exhaustion preserves partial work and is never PASS. Drafting the report early makes it recoverable.
facts.TERMINAL-CANCEL: A parent task cancellation may leave the child alive. Recheck the exact process before reading or cleaning its cwd.

p.QUOTA-DOMAINS: Concurrent processes using one credentialed launcher share that account's quota window. Another launcher or account has independent state but no presumed entitlement; probe it independently before real work.

p.NO-RETRY-WALL: On a known quota wall, preserve the worker cwd/report/diff and reroute the remaining bounded work. Do not retry against a published reset time or discard good artifacts because the runner exited nonzero.

p.VERSIONED-CALIBRATION: Model behavior belongs to the resolved version observed on that run. Historic GLM-5.2 evidence and current `glm-5.3[1m]` requests are not interchangeable claims. Use the capability playbooks as priors and update them from reviewed runs: @spec://org.vibevm.world/zai-glm-claude/flows/zai-glm-claude/playbooks/glm-big#root and @spec://org.vibevm.world/zai-glm-claude/flows/zai-glm-claude/playbooks/glm-turbo#root.

facts.RECOVERY-CENSUS: Inspect exact process state, cwd, visible diff, report and last event before taking action.
facts.RECOVERY-PRESERVE: A dead transport is not a code verdict. Preserve every unique artifact and classify which verification tail did not run.
facts.RECOVERY-CONTINUE: For a correctable defect, turn cap or stalled tail, prefer same-cwd continuation when its retained context makes repair cheaper. Otherwise write a fresh bounded packet for the remainder; do not blindly retransmit the original task.
facts.RECOVERY-KILL: Stop only the exact marked process or process chain. Never kill by broad executable name or unrelated task tree.
facts.CLEANUP: Remove a worker cwd/worktree only after its process is dead, product diff is accepted/rejected, durable findings have a home and no unique untracked artifact remains. Never prune registration while leaving a directory whose later `git -C` can retarget to an ancestor repository.

facts.ACCEPT-INVENTORY: Compare the actual changed-file set to the packet perimeter and report; classify every extra/missing path.
facts.ACCEPT-READ: Read the complete diff or artifact as a pull request against mandate and architecture.
facts.ACCEPT-REPRODUCE: Repeat the decisive narrow command with its real child exit and test count. A zero-test success is no proof.
facts.ACCEPT-MODEL: For a live provider test, separately verify terminal GLM model metadata and child session identity, ask the worker for its own exact model identity, and cross-check the two; do not infer execution identity from the launcher filename or requested alias.
facts.ACCEPT-NEGATIVE: Where false-green risk is material, run the named counterexample or mutation and restore it. The task packet may deliberately reduce this tier only by an explicit owner ruling; the final report then says reduced, never full.
facts.ACCEPT-DISPOSITION: Issue one explicit disposition: accept, same-cwd repair, recommission the remainder, or discard. Only then may integration or cleanup proceed.

harness-adapters.title: 13. Harness adapters

p.SETTINGS-ROOT-RESOLUTION: Both parent adapters resolve the configured VibeVM settings root: use `VIBE_SETTINGS` when set, otherwise the default `~/.vibe`. They never reconstruct an explicitly relocated settings root from the home directory.

p.CODEX-ADAPTER: Codex uses its process/terminal tool with `workdir` set to the worker cwd. It passes a short prompt pointer and observes the returned session/process id. It does not use a native subagent call when the requested worker is specifically the z.ai GLM lane.

p.CLAUDE-ADAPTER: Claude uses Bash or PowerShell from a scoped cwd and retains the exact process/session handle. The CLI spelling, packet and continuation law are otherwise identical.

p.ARGV-AND-EXIT: Do not insert a shell pipeline between a canonical PowerShell/Bash launcher and its exit capture. Redirect output first when needed, then capture the launcher child status immediately. Use the PowerShell launcher rather than the CMD convenience shim when exact Windows argument-vector preservation is part of the task.

p.PROVENANCE-POINTER: The source census, historical observations and contradictions resolved while forming this self-contained protocol are retained at @spec://org.vibevm.world/zai-glm-claude/flows/zai-glm-claude/provenance#root. Those records explain the rules; this protocol is the installed contract.
